scenes.text: Horses were sent to battle eels.
scenes.visual: Hot day on the Venezuelan plains, palms on the far bank: a bay horse stands belly-deep in a brown pond; an electric eel arches out of the water and presses its chin against the horse's flank; gold sparks pulse from the contact from the first frame, rings spread; a second eel glides under the surface.

scenes.text: In 1800, Alexander von Humboldt wanted live electric eels in Venezuela.
scenes.visual: Map of northern South America zooming in on Venezuela; Venezuela washes in; a red star marks Calabozo on the plains (Llanos), the Orinoco labelled.

scenes.text: So local men drove about thirty wild horses into a muddy pond.
scenes.visual: Wide sunny plain with palms: a herd of horses gallops in from the left and wades into a muddy pond, their legs vanishing under the brown water, rings and splashes spreading; two riders drive them from behind. Note 'about 30 horses'.

scenes.text: The eels rose, pressed against their bellies and fired, again and again.
scenes.visual: Closer on the water line: a chestnut horse belly-deep, whole in frame, seen from the other side; an eel rises out of the brown water on 'rose', its chin pressed against the horse's flank; on 'fired' gold sparks pulse from the contact again and again. Red note 'shock!'.
A big painted '2' on a water-blue swatch; above it a patch of brown pond water with rings spreading where something went under; hand-written under the number 'horses drowned'.

scenes.text: Then the tired eels were caught.
scenes.visual: A still, muddy pond, fully in frame, upright palms behind: on the left bank a plainsman in profile, straw hat, a coil of rope in his hand; the rope runs down to a harpoon shaft standing in the shallows beside a limp, exhausted eel, which is drawn slowly toward the bank; rings spread. Note 'harpoons on ropes'.

scenes.text: For two centuries, it sounded like a tall tale.
scenes.visual: A naturalist's diary page written in line by line: 'March 1800', 'thirty horses and mules', 'the eels pressed against them', 'two drowned', signed 'A. von Humboldt'.

scenes.text: In 2016, a biologist filmed eels leaping from the water to shock a threat.
scenes.visual: A lab: a glass tank on a table with low clear water; an aluminium plate with a column of small lights dips into it; an eel leaps up out of the water and presses its chin to the plate; on 'shock' the lights glow gold with each discharge. Note 'Vanderbilt lab, 2016'.
Dusk on the llanos: the pond calm and gold with the low sun, a single horse standing on the bank, palms dark against the sky; the picture slowly washes back to paper.

youtube.title: Electric Eels vs Horses: Did Humboldt Tell the Truth?
youtube.description:
Electric eels against horses sounds impossible: in March 1800, on the plains of Venezuela, Alexander von Humboldt wanted live electric eels, so local men drove about thirty wild horses and mules into a muddy pond. The eels rose, pressed against the horses and discharged again and again; two horses drowned within minutes, and only when the eels were exhausted could they be caught with harpoons on ropes. For two centuries scientists called it a tall tale, until biologist Kenneth Catania filmed electric eels leaping out of the water to shock a threat in 2016.
